messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — planning an RBAC change on the private-keystore svc tomorrow 09:00 UTC. This will rotate the ephemeral signing key and update service-account permissions. Wanted to call out impact on netpols and eviction scenarios.
Maya Patel: what's the exact change? will it touch the KMS policy or just local keystore?
Alex Chen: Only service-side key material will be rotated in the keystore agent; KMS master key unchanged. But we're adding a new role `keystore-reader` and removing broad `keystore-admin` from a few legacy svc-accounts.
Samir Gupta: can we see a diff of the RBAC? also need to confirm audit logging will capture failed decrypt attempts for the rotation window.
Alex Chen: attaching sample policy diff (local):
```
- roles/keystore-admin: svcaccs: [local-agent, legacy-agent]
+ roles/keystore-admin: svcaccs: [local-agent]
+ roles/keystore-reader: svcaccs: [rotation-worker, healthcheck]
```
Maya Patel: audit log retention question — private deploys currently ship logs to local ELK for 7d. For compliance we need 90d for any KMS-decrypt-fail events. ops-bot: @audit-bot will auto-forward events matching `kms.decrypt_failed` to secure-s3 in eu-west-1 for private regions? Please confirm.
ops-bot: Audit relay configured: forwarding disabled for private deploys unless `audit.forwarding.enabled=true` in customer control plane. Request a toggle via infra ticket.
Jordan Lee: If forwarding is disabled, we must ensure local forwarder is immutable and logs are write-once. Also netpols should not block forwarder egress to the ELK collector.
Maya Patel: netpol tweak needed: rotation-worker needs egress to metadata-proxy and to KMS endpoint (10.2.3.4:443). Current netpol denies outbound except to 10.0.0.0/8. Suggest add rule: allow to 10.2.3.4/32:443.
Samir Gupta: Is there any chance rotation triggers cascade evictions? e.g., if rotation-worker loses permission, keystore-agent may mark nodes unhealthy -> eviction.
Alex Chen: Risk exists. We've added a guardian path — if keystore TLS handshake fails x3, agent falls back to local cached key for 60s and triggers health-check only after 2m. That reduces false evictions.
Emily R: For incident response, add a playbook step: if >5 decrypt_failures/min across a cluster, pause rotation and open P1 runbook `priv-keystore-rotation-fail`.
Maya Patel: also need test plan for canary. Proposed: run rotation in a single AZ, monitor decrypt_failures, conntrack, pod restarts for 30m, then expand.
Samir Gupta: include `kubectl` checks in the playbook. e.g., `kubectl get pods -l app=keystore-agent -o json | jq '.items[].status.containerStatuses[].restartCount'`
Alex Chen: I'll create the infra PR with RBAC diff, netpol snippet, audit-forward toggle, and the runbook. Quick checklist:
- [ ] RBAC diff
- [ ] Netpol rule for rotation-worker
- [ ] Audit-forward toggle and retention config
- [ ] Fallback cache timeout set
- [ ] Canary plan and telemetry thresholds
Maya Patel: add acceptance criteria: zero evictions, decrypt_failures < 1/min, latency to KMS < 200ms.
ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled a dry-run: `deploy dry-run private-keystore 2024-05-02T09:00Z` (will only apply to canary AZ)
Jordan Lee: one more: ensure HSM/KMS rotation logs include key-version metadata so we can map decrypt failures to key versions in alerts.
Alex Chen: good catch. I'll add `key_version` tag to logs and to trace spans.
Samir Gupta: if anything goes sideways, incident commander should immediately switch routing to fallback model: route requests to hosted-keystore-proxy with read-only tokens.
Maya Patel: will update runbook. tagging @oncall-security for eyes.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone. I'll post the PR link here when ready.
Maya Patel: thx. ping when PR is up and I'll validate audit retention settings.
